why.pattern: A minting call shows where a key is made, not that it stays: a key held on an object can be replaced through setattr or a mapping (fixtures/premises/session_key_minted/planted), and a mint of too few bytes or of another module's function is a mint in name only.
why.established: The value is a library mint of at least 16 random bytes, assigned as written to a local of the function, which setattr cannot reach, with the library's module not rebound, patched or shadowed in the repository.
why.assumed: The query writes no fact when it finds no site, or one site it cannot prove, so map has nothing to read and keeps the pessimistic default.
why.unknown: Joern can be missing, crash or refuse a partial graph (kamanu.evidence.joern.JoernError): the query then has no answer, and the caller says so in map's unknown argument.

library_mint_in_local: The names secrets and uuid are the standard library's modules at run time
The caller cannot predict or set what the operating system's random source returns
Nothing replaces the key between the line that mints it and the engine that counts over it

redis_increment: Redis runs one command at a time
The name redis is the redis-py client at run time, and the server it reaches keeps every increment it has answered
Every process counts the same budget under the same key of that server
The check that admits a spend tests the answer of its own increment
